text:
maddie: Quick heads-up — started int4 conversion for Tangent9b to add to the catalogue. FP16 baseline OK, but int4 outputs show lower summarization scores and occasional repeated spans on long prompts. I pushed artifacts to s3.

vikram: Can you paste the exact convert command and one failing example from eval?

maddie: Convert command I used:
```bash
python tools/convert_model.py \\\
  --model tangent9b-fp16 \\\
  --out tangent9b-int4 \\\
  --quantizer int4_sym \\\
  --head-layout assumed_contiguous \\\
  --rotary-scale 1.0 \\\
  --export-kv-cache true
```
Failing eval example (from abstractive suite):
```
prompt_hash: 0x9f3a  rouge-l: 0.39  baseline: 0.48  truncated_repeat: true
```

ola: "assumed_contiguous" stands out. Some exporters for Tangent family use head-interleave layout. If we convert without remap, KV indices / rotary alignment will be off.

zane: Ran a quick kv index diff between FP16 and int4 on a short trace — saw token index drift starting around step 200 (longctx). snippet:
```
step 200: fp16_kv_index=4001  int4_kv_index=4002  offset=1
step 512: fp16_kv_index=1023  int4_kv_index=1023  offset=0
avg_offset: 0.12  max_offset:1
```

sam: Do we have the vocab manifest format for this export? Last time similar symptoms were a one-off indexing convention (exporter wrote 1-based ids). Applying vocab_shift=-1 fixed mapping.

maddie: Tried vocab_shift=-1, helps index drift (avg_offset -> 0.03) but summarization ROUGE still down ~4 pts. Also noticed rotary sin/cos matrices in a few layers differ slightly after quantization (L6.H3 mean delta ~0.0018).

vikram: That level of rotary perturbation can amplify under int4 noise. Which quant backend / kernel did you use? Symmetric kernels can bias small weights.

maddie: Default backend selected: int4_sym_native. Will re-run using int4_asym_adaptive and try head-permute remap path. Also will try headwise-rotary-scale=0.96 heuristic.

eva: Add failing prompts to Redwood Optimize as a regression set — we need automated checks for any model we add to hosted API.

infra-bot: artifact-uploader: s3://redwood-onboard/tangent9b/4832105555/ (convert.log, eval_samples.jsonl, kv_trace.parquet)

ola: Also add a kvcache smoke: run 3 repeats at longctx=8192 comparing logits at steps 256/512/1024 and dump L2 diffs. If drift accumulates only after a certain step, it points to head shuffle / kvcache index mapping.

zane: I put a tiny helper script in my fork: tools/kv_compare.py — usage: `python tools/kv_compare.py --a fp16 --b int4 --prompt long.txt --out diffs.json`. It shows per-step token id and logit l2.

maddie: Ran asym + head-permute remap + rotary_scale=0.96. Early results: avg token offset 0.02, max 0, rouge-l lifted from 0.39 -> 0.455 (baseline 0.48). Still short by ~2.5 pts but much better. kv_compare snippet:
```
step 256: offset 0  logit_l2: 0.0021
step 512: offset 0  logit_l2: 0.0036
```

sam: Good sign. Might be residual quant noise on attention outproj or layernorm folding differences. Try two more things: (1) calibrate per-channel scales for attention outproj, (2) try leaving rotary as fp16 (mixed precision for sin/cos tensors).

vikram: If mixed-precision sin/cos fixes quality without huge perf loss, we should add a conversion-profile flag for "rotary_fp16" and record perf tradeoffs. Also mark Tangent9b catalog entry with head-layout=interleaved.

eva: I'll open the onboarding ticket, mark `onhold` for Dedicated promotion until we hit <1.5 pt ROUGE delta on the regression set and add the failing prompts.

maddie: Will run per-channel calibration + rotary FP16 test and re-post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
